exclusions.reason: Identity owns application APIs, platform bindings, and final native and WebAssembly artifacts. Wallet supplies Rust libraries and canonical Wallet contracts.
Wallet-core emits typed lifecycle, consent, transaction, and presentation records. Native and web UI prompts, copy, accessibility behavior, and app navigation stay above this Rust crate.
OpenID4VCI protocol wire behavior belongs below wallet-core.
OpenID4VP protocol wire behavior belongs below wallet-core.
Credential envelope parsing and cryptographic validation stay below wallet-core.
The reallyme-wallet-zk integration crate names only reallyme-zk-api traits; concrete prover and verifier backends are injected by composed packages.

exclusions.owner: reallyme/ssi, reallyme/zk, identity, or wallet provider secure-area integrations
exclusions.reason: Wallet does not expose cryptographic pseudonym generation. Derivation, key material, and backend-specific proofs belong to the credential, proof, and secure-area providers.

exclusions.owner: reallyme/identity, wallet applications, and qualified trust service integrations
exclusions.reason: Wallet-core models QES/QSeal consent actions and digest-only QTSP decision records. Concrete QTSP account flows, remote signing activation, user prompts, and legal evidence packages are provider/application responsibilities.
Acquiring Wallet Instance and key attestations from the Wallet Provider stays above Wallet. Wallet verifies, binds, and rotates Wallet Unit Attestations through injected providers.
ISO/IEC 18013-5 transports and Digital Credentials API integration stay above Wallet. Wallet supplies reader-session consent receipts and contact-delivery framing.
Data-deletion requests to relying parties, reports to data protection authorities, and dashboard workflows are user-facing and stay above Wallet.
VaultWallet owns storage mechanics for authorized backup and migration. Wallet owns the authorization, lifecycle evidence, and portability policy.
